id: -2220-古提人對阿卡德帝國的突擊與征服
theater: 兩河中游阿卡德至蘇美爾

battle.name: 古提人對阿卡德帝國的突擊與征服
battle.theater: 兩河中游阿卡德至蘇美爾
battle.brief: 約公元前2220年，扎格羅斯山地的古提人順山道南下巴比倫尼亞，攻破並焚毀阿卡德都城，阿卡德帝國的霸權隨之瓦解；其後古提人又壓服南方蘇美爾諸城，直到烏提欣加爾與烏爾納姆相繼把他們逐出。卡面埃及長矛並未參戰，但它與阿卡德人手中的銅矛同屬早王朝以來最普遍的一支近身兵器。

kit.name: 埃及長矛
kit.history: 早王朝時期的長矛，銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上。埃及人用它守城垣，後來也用它收復失地。

countries: 這場戰爭的交戰方，不能用近代國家去套。北方一方是古提人：阿卡德語作 Guti-um 或 KUR a-a，蘇美爾王表稱之為「山中的古提人」，他們住在扎格羅斯山脈的兩翼，上游底格里斯河與卡爾特文的山間地帶，沒有王名留傳下來，只在阿卡德銘文中作為「高地的族群」出現。南方與中央的一方是阿卡德帝國——嚴格說是一個以薩爾貢建立的、由多族群拼成的王朝聯邦，都城在阿卡德，在蘇美爾另設烏魯與基什的舊行政中心。帝國的軍隊由王師（薩爾）與各城邦、各行省提供的徵發兵組成，行省總督（galli）與地方總督（ensi）分層節制，兵糧靠尼格羅河與人工運河供給。帝國崩解之後，蘇美爾的城邦重新立國：拉加什、烏瑪、埃什努納與所謂「海上地帶」各自為政；古提人佔據兩河中游與北部，成為蘇美爾城邦共同的壓迫者，也成為彼此爭奪灌溉地界的裁判。另有盧魯比人、圖魯庫人等山地族群，時而附從古提，時而與阿卡德人交鋒；阿卡德人自己的王表與宮廷史詩都把這些山民寫成需要反覆平定的邊患，而不是有國號的敵人。雙方的指揮系統也全然不同：阿卡德方有王名、官銜與成文的軍令，古提方靠部族首領與對山道的熟悉，一次突擊可以由數個氏族拼湊成臨時隊伍，勝負之後各自分散，沒有可以延續的編制。
countriesEn: The belligerents of this war cannot be fitted into modern categories. On the northern side stood the Gutians: Guti-um or KUR a-a in Akkadian, called by the Sumerian King List the Gutians of the mountain. They lived on both flanks of the Zagros, in the uplands of the upper Tigris and of the Kermanshah country, and they left no royal names behind them, appearing in Akkadian inscriptions simply as a highland people. On the central and southern side stood the Akkadian Empire, strictly speaking a dynasty-wide conglomerate of many peoples built by Sargon, with its capital at Akkad and older administrative centres at Ur and Kish in Sumer. Its army was made up of the royal host and of levies supplied by the cities and the provinces, controlled in layers by provincial governors (galli) and city governors (ensi), and supplied with grain and water by the Nigris and by artificial canals. Once the empire fell apart the Sumerian cities became states again: Lagash, Umma, Eshnunna and the so-called Sealand each governed itself, while the Gutians held the middle and upper valley of the two rivers and became at once the common oppressor of the Sumerian cities and the umpire of their quarrels over irrigation land. Other mountain peoples, such as the Lullubi and the Turukku, followed the Gutians at one moment and fought the Akkadians at another; Akkadian king lists and court literature alike describe these mountaineers as a frontier trouble to be put down again and again rather than as an enemy bearing a state name. The two command systems were entirely different. The Akkadian side had royal names, offices and written orders; the Gutian side rested on clan chiefs and on intimate knowledge of the mountain tracks, so that a raid could be thrown together for the occasion out of several kindreds, and after the fighting the groups dispersed without any establishment capable of outlasting it.
people: 留下名字的多是阿卡德人，古提方面幾乎無名。建國者薩爾貢（約前2334至前2279）以阿卡德為都，把分散的蘇美爾城邦收於王旗之下；里穆什（前2278至前2270）承其位而未能止住邊境壓力；馬尼什圖舒（前2270至前2255）在「偉大革命」中擊潰山地的古提與盧魯比，銘文提到古提人的首領扎爾維，並帶回「鷹」徽。帝國頂峰在那拉姆辛（前2254至前2218），他西征伊利德、盧魯比與西南伊朗，戰利品與銘文把帝國推到極盛，銅頭盔與戰勝碑便是那時的產物。末代君主沙爾卡利沙里（前2218至前2193）的稱號之一是「寬待古提人者」，說明古提曾被收編或撫平，也說明邊境必須靠這樣的寬宥維持。他死後帝國崩解。收拾殘局的是蘇美爾人：烏提欣加爾（約前2118至前2111）以「鷹」破古提人，維也納所藏凱旋碑即記此事（戰場所在文獻未載）；其後烏爾納姆（約前2112至前2095）建第三烏爾王朝，把古提人徹底逐出兩河，興建烏爾金字形神塔，並編纂蘇美爾王表。地方上，拉加什的烏魯卡基那宣稱打敗過古提與盧魯比，其子埃安納圖姆一世在與烏瑪的戰爭中記下海上地帶之王烏爾寧吉爾蘇與首領皮里格美。名號不見記載的古提王，僅在巴比倫王表殘片中留下「提茲阿塔爾」一名的斷片。
peopleEn: Those who left names behind were almost all Akkadians; on the Gutian side there are almost none. The founder Sargon (c. 2334-2279 BC) made Akkad his capital and gathered the scattered Sumerian cities under the royal banner; Rimush (2278-2270 BC) succeeded him without managing to arrest the pressure on the frontier; Manishtushu (2270-2255 BC) crushed the Gutians and the Lullubi in the Great Revolt, naming on his inscription the Gutian chief Zarwi and bringing back the emblem of the Eagle. The empire reached its height under Naram-Sin (2254-2218 BC), whose campaigns into Elam, against the Lullubi and towards south-western Iran pushed the empire to its furthest extent, and whose copper helmet and victory stele date from that time. The last ruler, Shar-Kali-Sharri (2218-2193 BC), carried among his titles that of the one who spares the people of Gutium, which shows that the Gutians had been taken into the empire or pardoned, and that the frontier had to be held by such acts of clemency. After his death the empire fell apart. The tidying up was done by Sumerians: Utu-hengal (c. 2118-2111 BC) broke the Gutians with the Eagle, and the Vienna stele of victory records the deed (the text does not give the battlefield); after him Ur-Nammu (c. 2112-2095 BC) founded the Third Dynasty of Ur, drove the Gutians out of the two rivers for good, raised the great ziggurat of Ur and drew up the Sumerian King List. In the cities, Urukagina of Lagash boasted of defeating the Gutians and the Lullubi, and his son Enannatum I, fighting Umma, set down the lord of the Sealand, Ur-Ningirsu, and the chief Pirig-me. The name of a Gutian king survives only as a broken fragment, Tiz-atal, in a tablet of the Babylonian King List.
kits: 卡面這支埃及長矛沒有出現在這場戰爭裡。它屬於早王朝時期（約前3200）埃及的裝備：銅或青銅矛頭綁在木杆上，埃及人用它守城垣、列陣，也用它收復失地，王室近衛與步兵方陣都以它為骨幹；它代表的是這段年代兵器工藝的水準——一把矛頭、一根木杆，人人都能備辦。真正在美索不達米亞打的是同一件東西的另一個版本：阿卡德士兵的基本武裝是銅矛（柄套式與鉞形矛頭各見）、銅戰斧、短匕首與鎚，遠射用弓，箭鏃有石、骨與青銅之別；防護靠木牌、皮革與銅牌，阿卡德式的方形銅盾見於尼普爾出土。將士與貴族用青銅盔，那拉姆辛的銅盔現藏於巴黎羅浮宮。車是四輪戰車，由野驢或驢牽引——當時美索不達米亞尚無馬匹，所以沒有騎兵，車只擔任指揮與衝擊。攻城靠圍城、斷糧、填壕與近牆強攻，器械只有木構的撞槌與土坡，沒有配重投石機。古提人的裝備簡陋得多：木杆矛、石鏃、投石索、柳條或皮盾，靠背囊與畜群自帶數日口糧，輕裝是他們的長處。古提人沒有攻城器械，本來也沒有攻城的打算，他們的目標是城外的倉廩、渠道與田園。
kitsEn: The Egyptian spear on the card took no part in this war. It belongs to the equipment of Egypt in the Early Dynastic period (c. 3200 BC): a copper or bronze head bound to a wooden shaft, used by the Egyptians to hold city walls, to form ranks and to recover lost ground, with the spear forming the backbone both of the royal guard and of the infantry line. It stands for the standard of armsmanship of its age - one head, one shaft, something every man could provide. What actually fought in Mesopotamia was another version of the same object: the basic kit of an Akkadian soldier was the copper spear, in both socketed and axe-head forms, with copper battle axes, short daggers and maces; missiles were shot from the bow, with stone, bone and bronze arrowheads; protection came from wooden shields, leather and copper, and the square copper shield of Akkadian type has been excavated at Nippur. Officers and nobles wore bronze helmets, and the copper helmet of Naram-Sin is in Paris in the Louvre. Vehicles were four-wheeled war wagons drawn by onagers or donkeys, for Mesopotamia still had no horses, so there were no cavalry at all and the wagon served only for command and shock. Siege work consisted of investment, cutting grain, filling the ditch and pressing close to the wall, with nothing but wooden rams and earthen ramps; there were no counterweight trebuchets. The Gutian equipment was far plainer: wooden-shafted spears, stone points, slings, wicker or hide shields, and rations carried on their own backs and pack animals, for lightness was their strength. The Gutians had no siege engines and had no intention of besieging anything; what they wanted was the granaries, the canals and the fields outside the walls.
tactics: 阿卡德人的遠征有一套成熟的樣板：馬尼什圖舒的偉大革命之役與那拉姆辛征盧魯比，都是先以大隊步兵與矛兵沿山道推進，戰車居中，弓手在陣後齊射，山地作戰靠分隊攀緣，奪下隘口與水源，再以屯駐迫使對方屈服；皇帝本人與「鷹」徽在陣前，士氣視之為神的護符。攻城則一律圍而不強攻，斷其渠壩、焚其田禾，等城內斷糧自潰，必要時填壕逼近牆根。帝國結構本身也影響打法：一切都靠從蘇美爾城邦徵來的兵與糧，戰線拉得越長，供給線越脆。古提人的戰術正相反。他們不與阿卡德人爭奪隘口，而是趁阿卡德主力遠征或中央空虛時，一次集結順山谷而下：步兵在前面放箭與投石，輕裝急行，進城即破門而入，隨即破壞倉廩、渠道、橋樑與碼頭，切斷北方物資南下與南方穀物北上的路線，再退回山地以免被黏住。他們熟悉季節的水情，選在春天河道漲水、道路泥濘而阿卡德重車難行的時節南下。占領之後並不設防禦工事，只維持對城市與鄉村的掠奪性控制。蘇美爾城邦的應對是守住城牆、挖深護城河，並在城邦之間結盟：拉加什與烏瑪為爭運河地界打了數十年，最後由烏爾納姆以新王朝把它們一併收編。古提時期因此既是城邦競逐的高峰，也是城邦結盟的高峰。
tacticsEn: The Akkadians had a settled pattern for campaigning. The Great Revolt of Manishtushu and Naram-Sin's war against the Lullubi both began with masses of foot and spearmen moving along the mountain tracks, the wagons in the centre, archers loosing volleys in the rear; in the hills they worked by parties climbing to seize passes and water sources, and then stood camped to force the enemy to yield. The king himself and the emblem of the Eagle went in front, and the troops read that as a god's protection. When a city was met they invested it and did not storm it, cutting its canals and burning its crops and waiting for it to starve, filling the ditch and closing on the wall only when they had to. The structure of the empire shaped the fighting as well: everything rested on men and grain levied from the Sumerian cities, so the longer the front, the more brittle the line of supply. The Gutian method was the exact opposite. They did not contest the passes for possession; they came down the valleys in a single concentration, at the moment when the Akkadian army was far away in the field or the centre was empty: skirmishers ahead with bows and slings, the rest moving light and fast, breaking in at the gate and then destroying granaries, canals, bridges and landing stages, so as to cut both the flow of northern goods southward and of southern grain northward, and then withdrawing back into the mountains rather than be held there. They knew the seasonal water, and chose the spring, when the channels were in flood and the roads were mud and the heavy Akkadian wagons could not move. Once they had taken a place they built no works of defence and kept only a predatory grip on the towns and the countryside. The Sumerian cities answered by holding their walls, deepening their moats and allying with each other: Lagash and Umma fought over canal boundaries for decades, until Ur-Nammu absorbed them both into his new dynasty. The Gutian period was therefore at once the high point of city-state rivalry and the high point of city-state alliance.
data: 這場戰爭的可核數字極少，只能分成三類。第一類是年代：中部年代學把薩爾貢的統治放在前2334至前2279，那拉姆辛前2254至前2218，沙爾卡利沙里前2218至前2193，阿卡德的陷落約在前2190（另一些表列前2150），古提時期延續到前2050上下；短年代學把整段前移約一百年。戰爭列表所採的 -2220 落在兩套體系之間，也可能是取那拉姆辛死後中央失控的時刻，確切年份無法從文本復原。蘇美爾王表在沙爾卡利沙里之後寫「阿卡德王國被取去，古提人開國」，而古提時期的諸王名多已殘缺，僅一兩片殘簡可讀。第二類是考古：伊利德（蘇薩）於1940年出土那拉姆辛的銅盔與戰勝碑，1947年皮爾侯森出土那拉姆辛碑、達爾班德-加烏爾出土沙爾卡利沙里的碑，說明帝國末期的紀念建築遍布兩河中游；泰拉塔亞有被定為古提時期的地層與大柱廳；泰勒萊蘭、泰勒布拉克等地的前2200年前後破壞層，可與帝國崩解互相對照。第三類是只能推估的量：阿卡德帝國的疆域涵蓋今伊拉克大部，總人口被估在百萬量級而爭議很大；古提遠征的兵力無任何記載，僅知其足以攻破帝都並長期佔住中北部；巴比倫到扎格羅斯山麓的直線距離約四百至五百公里，一支以步行為主的遠征隊伍往返一趟要耗掉數月口糧。阿卡德方面的兵員、陣亡與攻城器械數量，全部無案可查。
dataEn: The checkable numbers for this war are very few and fall into three classes. The first is chronology. Middle chronology puts Sargon's reign at 2334-2279 BC, Naram-Sin at 2254-2218 BC and Shar-Kali-Sharri at 2218-2193 BC, places the fall of Akkad at about 2190 BC (some lists give 2150 BC), and lets the Gutian period run to around 2050 BC; short chronology moves the whole sequence forward by about a century. The -2220 used in the list of wars falls between the two systems, and may also be taken as the moment of the loss of central control after the death of Naram-Sin, for the exact year cannot be recovered from the texts. The Sumerian King List says, after Shar-Kali-Sharri, that the kingdom of Akkad was taken away and the reign of the Gutians began, and the royal names of the Gutian period are mostly broken, only one or two fragments remaining legible. The second class is archaeological. In 1940 at Susa in Elam the copper helmet of Naram-Sin and his victory stele were excavated; in 1947 the Naram-Sin stele came to light at Pir Hüseyin and the stele of Shar-Kali-Sharri at Darband-i-Gawr, which shows that commemorative building of the late empire was spread across the middle valley; Tell Taya has a layer assigned to the Gutian period with its great hypostyle hall; and the destruction levels of about 2200 BC at Tell Leilan and Tell Brak can be set beside the collapse of the empire. The third class is estimate only. The territory of the Akkadian Empire covered most of modern Iraq, and its total population is put in the order of a million, though the figure is much disputed; the strength of the Gutian raid is nowhere recorded, and all that is known is that it was enough to break the imperial capital and to hold the middle and upper country for a long time; the straight-line distance from Babylon to the foot of the Zagros is about four hundred to five hundred kilometres, so a marching army on foot needed months of rations for one round trip. The numbers of Akkadian troops, of casualties and of siege machines are simply not to be found.
cause: 打起來的原因有四層。第一層是帝國擴張本身：薩爾貢把王都從蘇美爾的烏魯搬到中部的阿卡德，又沿扎格羅斯山麓與西南伊朗一路掠取木材、銅、銀與獸皮，越是把勢力伸進山地，越要與古提、盧魯比這些高原族群正面相撞；那拉姆辛本人就死在把這條邊界推得更遠的戰役裡。第二層是中央與地方的裂痕：阿卡德帝國靠向蘇美爾城邦攤派兵員與稅賦維持，都城權力愈強，地方愈怨，那拉姆辛晚年的烏瑪起義（署名「古伽拉納，奴僕那拉姆辛」的印章是這次叛亂最著名的物證）就說明帝國並未把蘇美爾人心服。第三層是地理與補給：從山區南下的戰線越拉越長，糧草要靠尼格羅河、人工運河與驢車輸送，而美索不達米亞沒有馬，車靠野驢拖，越野作戰與追擊都極吃力；那拉姆辛對盧魯比的遠征雖勝，卻把帝國最精銳的部隊帶到無法及時回援的深山。第四層是繼承與權威：沙爾卡利沙里的統治靠寬宥邊民維持，帝國末期王室的號令力已經不足，一旦中央主力遠離或空虛，山地的破口就再也擋不住。
causeEn: There were four layers of reason behind the war. The first is the expansion of the empire itself. Sargon moved the royal capital from Ur in Sumer to Akkad in the middle country, and then took timber, copper, silver and hides along the foot of the Zagros and into south-western Iran; the further the reach extended into the highlands, the more directly it collided with the plateau peoples such as the Gutians and the Lullubi, and Naram-Sin himself died in the battle that pushed that frontier further out. The second layer is the fissure between centre and localities. The Akkadian Empire maintained itself by levying men and taxes on the Sumerian cities; the stronger the power of the capital grew, the more the provinces resented it, and the rising in Umma in the last years of Naram-Sin - the seal inscribed with the name of Gugalana, servant of Naram-Sin, is the best-known relic of that revolt - shows that the empire had not won the loyalty of Sumer. The third layer is geography and supply. A front coming down out of the mountains kept lengthening, the grain had to travel by the Nigris, by artificial canal and by donkey cart, and Mesopotamia had no horses, the wagons being drawn by onagers, so that campaigning across country and pursuit were both extremely hard; Naram-Sin's expedition against the Lullubi won, but it carried the best of the imperial troops deep into mountains from which they could not be recalled in time. The fourth layer is succession and authority. The government of Shar-Kali-Sharri was held together by the clemency he extended to the frontier peoples, and by the end of the empire the royal word was no longer strong enough; once the main body of the army was far away or absent, the breach in the mountains could not be closed again.
impact: 這場戰爭帶來的第一個結果是帝國的消失，而它的深遠影響卻不在戰場上。阿卡德城被焚，帝國的行政體系、灌溉管理、常備軍與行省制度一併瓦解，蘇美爾各城邦回到各自為政的時代：拉加什、烏瑪、埃什努納、海上地帶輪流做兩河中游的主人，灌溉地界的爭端成為城邦之間最長久的戰爭，也催生了留下姓名的城邦英雄埃安納圖姆一世與他的紀功碑。第二，阿卡德王朝留下的文化記憶成為往後千年的基準：那拉姆辛的宮廷被視為黃金時代的頂點，其後是「沒有王名」的黑暗，蘇美爾王表與巴比倫王表都以古提時期作為分水嶺，後世的城市國家作者在描述自己的時代時，常常借古提人說明「蠻族入主」這件事在近東政治記憶裡的位置。第三，行政與技術沒有消失，而是分散到各城邦，並在約半個世紀後由第三王朝的烏爾納姆重新收攏：編王表、興神塔、重整秩序，逐漸為後來古巴比倫的集權鋪路。第四，考古學的損失至今無法彌補：阿卡德都城的遺址從未被確定，帝國的宮殿、文書與器物只能靠文本推想，因此這場戰爭的細節，包括古提人究竟有多少、走哪幾條山道、攻城用了什麼手段，都仍然是空白。
impactEn: The first result of this war was the disappearance of the empire, yet its deeper consequences lay elsewhere than on the battlefield. Akkad was burned, and with it the administrative system, the irrigation management, the standing army and the provincial machinery of the empire collapsed; the Sumerian cities returned to a time of separate governments. Lagash, Umma, Eshnunna and the Sealand in turn became the masters of the middle valley, disputes over irrigation land became the longest wars between cities, and they produced the one city-state hero whose name has survived, Enannatum I, together with his stele of victory. Second, the cultural memory left by the Akkadian dynasty became the measure for a thousand years to come: the court of Naram-Sin was held to be the summit of a golden age, and after it came a darkness of unrecorded kings; both the Sumerian King List and the Babylonian King List take the Gutian period as a watershed, and later authors describing their own age in the city states borrowed the Gutians to show what the coming in of a barbarian host meant in the political memory of the Near East. Third, administration and technique did not vanish but were distributed among the cities, and about half a century later Ur-Nammu of the Third Dynasty gathered them in again, drawing up the king list, raising the ziggurat and reordering affairs, which paved the way for the centralisation of Old Babylon. Fourth, the archaeological loss cannot be made good: the site of the city of Akkad has never been identified, and the palaces, the documents and the objects of the empire can only be imagined from texts, so that the details of this war - how many Gutians there were, which tracks they used, what they did against the walls - remain blank.
result: 結果可以分三段講。第一段是古提人的突擊成功：阿卡德城被攻破並焚毀，帝國的政令系統在美索不達米亞中北部中斷，蘇美爾城邦淪為被掠奪的地區，古提人佔據兩河中游約數十年。第二段是古提人的失敗：他們能打下城市，卻建不起國家，沒有水利的重建，沒有文字的官僚，沒有穩定的稅收，也沒有辦法同時壓住南方的十幾個城邦；拉加什與烏瑪的戰爭、海上地帶的獨立、阿卡德殘餘貴族的反抗，把古提人拖在無法收拾的局面裡；蘇美爾王表把這段時期記為一連串沒有王名的空檔，正說明統治權在這一百年裡不斷易手。第三段是收束：烏提欣加爾擊潰古提人，烏爾納姆繼而把他們逐出兩河，建立第三王朝，築起烏爾的金字形神塔，並把這段被抹去的歷史寫進王表的最後幾行。結果可以這樣概括：古提人贏得了對阿卡德帝國的征服，卻輸掉了對蘇美爾的征服；帝國時代結束，城邦時代開始，而城邦時代的版圖，最終由重新集權的烏爾第三王朝收回到自己手裡。
resultEn: The result can be told in three movements. The first is the success of the Gutian raid: Akkad was taken and burned, the administrative order of the empire was broken in the middle and upper Euphrates-Tigris valley, the Sumerian cities were reduced to a country to be plundered, and the Gutians held the middle river country for some decades. The second is the failure of the Gutians: they could take cities but could not build a state. They had no reconstruction of the irrigation works, no bureaucracy of the written word, no steady revenue, and no way of holding down a dozen southern cities at once; the war between Lagash and Umma, the independence of the Sealand and the resistance of the surviving Akkadian nobility dragged them into a situation they could not manage, and the Sumerian King List records this stretch as a series of blanks with no royal name in them, which shows precisely how constantly the right to rule changed hands during that century. The third movement is the closing of the account: Utu-hengal broke the Gutians, Ur-Nammu then drove them out of the two rivers, founded the Third Dynasty, raised the ziggurat of Ur and wrote this suppressed stretch of history into the last lines of the king list. The result can be put in one sentence: the Gutians won the conquest of the Akkadian Empire and lost the conquest of Sumer; the age of empire ended, the age of the city states began, and the map of that city-state age was gathered back into the hands of a reunited Ur in the Third Dynasty.
